note: Rated endurance and known advisories, keyed by model family. Figures are taken from the vendor's own datasheet or support page, named in each entry's `source` — check it before acting on a number, and prefer your drive's own reported wear where it has one. This table is deliberately short: an entry nobody can verify is worse than a missing one, because a missing one says so. Add your own in Settings, or edit this file and point the refresh URL at your copy.

drives.notes: TBW scales with capacity; the 1 TB figure is the one usually quoted. The drive reports its own wear indicator, which is the better number to watch.

advisories.title: Early firmware; a later revision is available
advisories.detail: Samsung has shipped firmware updates for this family since launch. Updating is a maintenance action rather than a fix for a specific defect, so it is informational: check the current version on Samsung's support page if you have never updated the drive.

drives.notes: NVMe, so the drive reports percentage_used directly and this is only a cross-check.
Not the 980 PRO — that is a different family with higher ratings.

drives.source: Western Digital Red datasheet; WD's 2020 statement on SMR in the Red line
drives.notes: These are the Red models WD shipped with shingled magnetic recording without saying so at launch. They work as single drives and are a poor choice in a RAID array, where a rebuild can take days and time out.

advisories.title: SMR drive in a Red line that was sold as RAID-ready
advisories.detail: Shingled recording rewrites neighbouring tracks, so sustained random writes are far slower than the drive's sequential speed suggests. In a RAID array that shows up as a rebuild that runs for days or drops out entirely. Western Digital confirmed the models and published a compatibility note after the fact. Check WD's current guidance before putting one of these in a pool.

drives.notes: Rated workload, not a total: this is how much data the drive is expected to move per year for its warranty to stand.
A desktop drive. Fine as one drive, and the workload rating is why it is not the drive to put in an array.
